# Postify

> Verified knowledge for developers: practical technical writing with explicit evidence and freshness signals.

## Trust semantics
- `Author tested` means the author claims to have tested the guidance in the displayed environment. It is not an independent Postify execution.
- Authenticated `Worked / Didn't work` feedback on canonical posts is stored as the contributor's private confirmation and contributes only to privacy-safe community aggregates. Anonymous or fallback feedback stays device-local.
- Community success percentages are withheld until at least 3 independent confirmations exist; smaller samples show counts without an inflated rate.
- `Postify verified` means the displayed checked-in deterministic code exactly matched the release manifest, executed successfully, and its runtime freshness is still current.
- Runtime freshness is checked against the official Node.js release signal. A newer LTS release or an unavailable freshness signal withholds the current Verified badge while preserving the historical execution artifact.
- Automatic verification is policy-limited checked-in execution, not a sandbox for arbitrary or untrusted user code.

## Content types
- Guide: accomplish a concrete task.
- Decision note: compare choices and trade-offs.
- Explainer: understand a concept.
- Field note: report lessons from real work.

## Canonical site
https://postify.zekiakgul.dev/

## Machine-readable trust artifacts
- `/verification-runs.json`: exact executed code/runtime/output/hash contract.
- `/runtime-release-status.json`: current/re-check/unknown runtime freshness signal.
- `/knowledge/<slug>.<locale>.json`: canonical article evidence plus execution and runtime-release binding.
